newsitem.title: USA: Fox/Liberty Networks to sell $600 mln junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Fox/Liberty Networks to sell $600 mln junk bonds.

text.p: Fox/Liberty Networks plans to sell $600 million in junk bonds to finance its purchase of a 40 percent equity interest in the sports holdings of Rainbow Media Holdings Inc, according to market sources.
Merrill Lynch & Co will lead manage the two-part 144A private placement which will consist of $350 million in 10-year senior notes and $250 million in 10-year senior discount notes.
Market sources said Fox/Liberty has also arranged a $900 million bank facility and term loan via a Chase Manhattan Corp and Toronto-Dominion Bank -led syndicate.

In June, Fox/Liberty agreed to buy a 40 percent equity interest in Rainbow Media's regional sports networks for $850 million. Sources close to the situation expected that transaction to close by the end of August.
Fox/Liberty is a joint venture between News Corp's Fox Sports unit and Liberty Media Corp, a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
Rainbow is 75 percent owned by Cablevision Systems Corp and 25 percent owned by General Electrics Co's NBC unit.
Rainbow Media's sports networks currently operate under the brand name of SportsChannel.
In June, Fox/Liberty and Rainbow also agreed to form an equally-owned national sports programming network under the brand name, FOX Sports Net, which the companies claim will reach 55 million homes.
In addition to its large size, Fox/Liberty Network's junk bond offering was notable because it will be one of the first to come from a pure television programming company, market sources said.
The roadshow for the offering will begin on Wednesday. The deal is expected to be priced in mid-August, sources said.
-- Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-859-1662
